title: Post-Course Portfolio: Blog Backend
descriptionMarkdown:
# Blog Backend

## Position in the curriculum

Post-course portfolio: build after finishing the full curriculum through the final capstone, and after (or alongside) the simpler URL Shortener/Notes Web App entries. This is the first catalog entry with a genuine entity relationship (a post has many comments), which is exactly where N+1 queries and lazy-fetching mistakes first become possible.

## What is graded, and what is external

This project has a dedicated, automatically-graded checkpoint: **`blog-moderation-checkpoint`** ("Post and comment moderation"), a pure in-memory `BlogModeration.run(String input)` program implementing exactly the post/comment/hide/visible-count moderation core. Passing its hidden tests proves your moderation-state rules are correct.

The real relational mapping — an actual `Post`-to-`Comment` one-to-many JPA relationship, and the N+1 query problem that comes with it — cannot be graded by a pure in-memory sandbox test, since there is no real SQL being generated. That is exactly what the Required Evidence's SQL-logging exercise, run against your own database, is for.

## Architecture overview

```text
PostController                 <- create/list/get post, add comment
PostService                     <- your checkpoint's moderation rules, reshaped as a Spring bean
Post (JPA entity)                <- id, title, author, @OneToMany(mappedBy="post", fetch=LAZY) comments
Comment (JPA entity)              <- id, @ManyToOne post, body, hidden
PostResponse / CommentResponse   <- DTOs assembled from the entity graph, never the entities themselves
```

## Build it as vertical slices

1. **Slice 1 — port the checkpoint logic into a service.** Carry your post/comment/hide/visible-count rules into `PostService`, unit tests unchanged.
2. **Slice 2 — the JPA mapping.** Create `Post` and `Comment` with a `LAZY` one-to-many relationship and a migration for both tables.
3. **Slice 3 — reproduce the N+1 problem on purpose.** Write an endpoint that lists posts and, for each, accesses `.getComments().size()`; enable SQL logging and observe one query per post.
4. **Slice 4 — fix it with `JOIN FETCH`.** Add a dedicated repository query for the one endpoint that actually needs comments eagerly, and confirm via SQL logging that the query count drops to one.
5. **Slice 5 — moderation and visibility.** Add the `HIDE` operation and make sure a post's visible comment count (and a comment listing endpoint) excludes hidden comments, exactly as your checkpoint already proved correct in isolation.

## Common pitfalls

- **"Fixing" N+1 by switching the relationship to `EAGER` globally.** This just moves the cost to every load of a `Post`, even the majority that never need comments; fix it per-query with `JOIN FETCH` or `@EntityGraph` instead.
- **Serializing the `Post` entity directly, with its `comments` collection, as the response.** This risks a `LazyInitializationException` once the transaction closes, and leaks internal entity structure; always translate to a DTO within the transactional boundary.
- **Hiding a comment by deleting it instead of marking it hidden.** The checkpoint's own contract distinguishes "hidden" (still exists, doesn't count) from "gone"; deleting loses the moderation history.
- **Forgetting that `commentId` uniqueness is global, not scoped to a post**, exactly as your checkpoint's tests require — reusing a `commentId` under a different post must be rejected.

## How to self-test what the checkpoint cannot reach

- Enable `spring.jpa.show-sql=true` (or a proper SQL logger), hit the list-posts-with-comment-counts endpoint before and after adding `JOIN FETCH`, and count the actual queries in the log.
- Fetch a post's full detail view, close the underlying transaction (call the service method from a `@Transactional`-free test), and confirm you get a clean DTO rather than a `LazyInitializationException`.
- Hide a comment via the API, then GET the post and confirm the visible count decreased by exactly one while the comment still exists in a direct repository lookup.

## Required evidence

- SQL-logging evidence (before and after) showing the N+1 query pattern and its fix reducing the query count for the same endpoint.
- A `@DataJpaTest` for the `JOIN FETCH` query confirming it returns posts with comments populated in one round trip.
- A test confirming a post's DTO never accidentally exposes the author's internal entity fields (only the fields the DTO declares).
- A `@WebMvcTest` for the comment-creation endpoint's validation (a blank comment body is rejected with 400).
- A short written note explaining, for one specific endpoint, why `LAZY` is the right default and why that one endpoint specifically needed `JOIN FETCH` instead.

## Review and completion

A reviewer asks you to add a `GET /api/posts` list endpoint and predicts, before you write it, whether your existing entity mapping will produce an N+1 query for it — then checks your SQL log to see if the prediction was right and, if so, asks you to fix it the same way.
learningObjectives: Complete the graded post/comment moderation checkpoint and carry its verified rules into a real one-to-many JPA relationship
Reproduce a genuine N+1 query with SQL logging, then fix it with JOIN FETCH for exactly the endpoint that needs it
Keep response DTOs separate from entities across a relationship, not just a single flat entity
Apply Bean Validation to a nested creation request (a comment attached to a post)
Distinguish hiding content from deleting it, and enforce global uniqueness across a two-entity id namespace
